stem:
Heena compares $x^{2}+y^{2}=z^{2}$ with $x^{n}+y^{n}=z^{n}$ for integers $n>2$.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: Both equations are Baudhāyana triples under one shared name.
Solutions for $n>2$ are what produce the square-power triples, rather than the square case being the one with triples.
Positive natural-number solutions exist for the square case, but not when $n>2$.
The equations match because both print a plus sign between powers.

teacher.key_rationale: Baudhāyana triples solve the square-power equation. Fermat's Last Theorem rules out positive solutions for n>2. Merging both under one name, reversing which case has solutions, or matching on a printed plus sign all miss that hinge.
